items.title: Rob Lowe Claps Back at Criticism of His Choice to Work With Ben Shapiro
items.summary:
Rob Lowe is standing by his decision to work with Ben Shapiro — despite attracting some backlash for the call.

Speaking on the “Second Thought” podcast this week, Lowe, 62, defended starring in Confession , a psychological historical drama written by Shapiro, 42, who is known for his right-wing political views.

Lowe insisted that he took on the project because he was more interested in the script than the politics surrounding its writer.

“It’s a really, really, really interesting assessment of not only where our world is, but where Hollywood is as well,” Lowe said on the podcast. “So, I read the script. It was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’”

Rob Lowe Congratulated Bradley Cooper for Robert Downey Jr.'s Golden Globe 

Lowe said Shapiro initially asked whether he knew a leading man in his 50s who wouldn’t be intimidated by the idea of working with him. Lowe was quick to volunteer himself.

“And I go, ‘Yeah, me,’” Lowe recalled telling Shapiro, adding that he was comfortable taking on the role.

Lowe continued, “And he goes, ‘You’re good with it?’ I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’”

Rob Lowe. (Photo by Cindy Ord/Getty Images) 
 Confession , which is directed by Václav Marhoul , follows the interrogation of a prisoner in a Stalin-era Russian jail. The film also stars Nick Nolte, James Franco and Emile Hirsch .

The film premiered at the Warsaw Film Festival in October, then received a one-night-only theatrical release on November…
items.t: Rob Lowe Claps Back at Criticism of His Choice to Work With Ben Shapiro

The former professional player, whose career spanned more than two decades, died of heart disease at age 83 at his Las Vegas home in September 2024. Prior to his death, Rose pleaded guilty in 1990 to two felony counts of filing false federal tax income returns, for which he served five months in prison.

Rose, the all-time hits leader in Major League Baseball history, became a superstar with the Reds from 1963 to 1978. He would later return to the Reds in 1984 and play the final three seasons of his professional career with the franchise, when he also acted as a player-manager for the team until 1989.
